mentions.name: zfetch
mentions.description: zfetch is a single static binary that fetches URLs over HTTPS with strict security defaults, intended to replace curl in restricted environments where a small, auditable tool with no runtime dependencies is needed. It is also usable as a Zig library for embedding HTTP(S) fetches in other programs, and it vendors and links BoringSSL.
mentions.problem: In restricted environments, existing tools like curl are not small or auditable and come with runtime dependencies.
mentions.audience: For applications and teams working in restricted environments that need a small, auditable HTTP fetch tool with no runtime dependencies; also developers embedding HTTP(S) fetches in their own programs.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Me and Claude have been working on zfetch (https://github.com/roobie/zfetch), which is a single static binary that fetches URLs over HTTPS with strict security defaults. For many applications, it should be able to replace curl in restricted environments where you need a small, auditable tool with no runtime dependencies.

It should also be usable as a Zig library for embedding HTTP(S) fetches in your own programs.
